description: This paper record from the IRD documentation service evaluates the Raincell App, a demonstrator for early warning of flash floods in Bamako, Mali, using the flood of 16 May 2019 as a test. Nanee Chahinian and colleagues found that none of the global forecasting systems foresaw the intense rainfall or its size, while the hydrological model behind the app correctly located most of the places where rivers overflowed. They recommend adding two-dimensional hydraulic modelling, installing discharge and water level sensors next to the existing rain monitoring and educating communities about keeping waterways unblocked. The article appeared in the Journal of Flood Risk Management, volume 16, issue 3, in 2023; the record page is free to read and states no licence. Coverage is one city and one event. The evaluation report is available online as a document. Caveats: only the bibliographic record was read, not the full text, so data and model details are those summarised on the record. For simulation, it is a documented case for emergency response and flood hazard exposure modelling in West African cities. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.

outcomes: On 16 May 2019 an unexpected intense rainfall event caused severe flooding in Bamako while the Raincell App demonstrator was still in development; no global forecasting system foresaw its size, but the hydrological model correctly identified most locations where overbank flow occurred, and the authors recommend two-dimensional hydraulic modelling, discharge and water level sensors and community education on keeping waterways clear.
